summary: P10 iteration 2 passes the keep gate under the platform verification discipline (Windows dev host + native macOS CI; no WSL, no cross-target). The macOS gate is kernel-held: one posix_spawn call under POSIX_SPAWN_START_SUSPENDED | POSIX_SPAWN_SETPGROUP(0) | POSIX_SPAWN_CLOEXEC_DEFAULT means not one workload instruction can precede the guardian's SIGCONT after a valid Release — strictly stronger than a pre-exec stop (no fork, no pre-exec window). Birth identity is the PROC_PIDTBSDINFO tuple read via libc::proc_pidinfo into a size-pinned repr(C) ProcBsdInfo (XNU layout), fail-closed, re-probed daemon-side and matched before handout; zero /proc dependency (no sysctl/KERN_PROC shortcuts — pinned by tests). The P08 session state machine and protocol codec are reused verbatim (exit codes 0/1/2); release_once(self) is exactly-once by construction; an unreleased Drop SIGKILLs the still-suspended group; CLOEXEC_DEFAULT pins the inherited fd set to exactly {0,1,2}. Honest scope: the guardian runs as a bounded in-process thread — the cross-process guardian binary (daemon-death propagation) is P24H's contract, and the session is stream-generic so that binary is a thin fd wrapper. QA's deep review independently verified every libc 0.2.189 apple binding claim against vendored source and re-derived the 136-byte layout; s10 (13 tests) and the 4 macos.rs unit tests execute in native macOS CI and were never counted as locally run.
